C1.rationale: Teamwork, de-escalation communication, stakeholder engagement, and communicating socially just responses to crime to diverse community audiences (CILOs).
evidenceLines: work independently and as part of a team to compare and contrast a number of approaches to crime across different cultural, historical and geographical settings;
apply skills to construct and communicate effectively, a variety of socially just responses to crime to different audiences;

C2.rationale: Requires intellectual originality to formulate innovative crime prevention frameworks and policy responses addressing complex local and global criminality (CILOs).
evidenceLines: demonstrate sophisticated knowledge of models of engaging government and wider society to improve responses to crime and criminality;
apply knowledge of contemporary criminological concerns to understand and examine crime and responses to crime at the local, national and international level;

C3.rationale: Critical analysis of criminal etiology, statutory criminal law provisions, evidentiary standards, and systemic limits of criminal justice interventions (Overview, CILOs).
evidenceLines: Through core units you will develop a critical understanding of crime, the broader context in which crime occurs, the drivers of criminal behaviour, and the limits of formal and informal responses to crime.
apply practical skills and knowledge of law curriculum acquired at the police academy;

C4.rationale: Adapts policing and criminological frameworks dynamically in high-stakes operational environments, crisis situations, and changing community contexts (Overview, CILOs).
evidenceLines: Through core units you will develop a critical understanding of crime, the broader context in which crime occurs, the drivers of criminal behaviour, and the limits of formal and informal responses to crime.
identify, define and describe key global challenges to crime and responses to crime;

C5.rationale: Intensive physical presence, tactical field training, physical restraint/defense skills, and operational exercises at the Victoria Police Academy (Overview, CILOs).
evidenceLines: apply practical skills and knowledge of law curriculum acquired at the police academy;
In a joint-venture with Victoria Police, the Bachelor of Criminology and Policing is the only course of its kind in Victoria.

W1.rationale: Direct workplace integration through the Victoria Police Academy, operational police mentoring, and concurrent Diploma of Policing studies (Overview).
evidenceLines: If accepted, during the third year of your course, you will undertake studies which will allow you to complete your bachelor degree and concurrently commence a Diploma of Policing with Victoria Police. You will also be allocated a Victoria Police mentor who will support and guide you during your Diploma studies and your journey into the police force .
apply practical skills and knowledge of law curriculum acquired at the police academy;

W2.rationale: Rigorous professional policing ethics, procedural justice, statutory accountability, and integrity standards governing sworn officers (CILOs, Overview).
evidenceLines: apply skills to construct and communicate effectively, a variety of socially just responses to crime to different audiences;
engage in the scholarship of professional practice to effectively respond to crime prevention and issues of crime.

W3.rationale: Direct training in statutory police powers, law enforcement databases, criminal procedure legislation, and operational police equipment (CILOs, Overview).
evidenceLines: apply practical skills and knowledge of law curriculum acquired at the police academy;
